cases.prompt: Design how to delegate our weekly vendor invoice intake. Observed run on 2026-09-21: AP clerk Elena opens the shared AP inbox, downloads about 60 PDF invoices, finds each vendor in NetSuite by VAT number, matches PO number and amount against the open PO (2% tolerance), enters matches as 'pending approval' bills, and forwards mismatches to purchasing. Finance controller Tomas approves the payment run every Thursday. Failures today: about 3 duplicates a week, caught by NetSuite's duplicate invoice-number check; about 5 scanned invoices a week have unreadable totals and are keyed manually. Authority: only Tomas approves payments; Elena may create pending bills. Detection: NetSuite audit log and a weekly reconciliation report.
sourceAnchors: Separate lookup, parsing, validation, routing, and invariant enforcement that can be deterministic from synthesis or classification that needs judgment.
Put checkpoints immediately before the smallest irreversible or externally visible action.

requiredEvidence: unreadable scans fall back to a human
idempotency key on vendor and invoice number
forbiddenActions: schedule the agent to approve payment runs

cases.prompt: Write the Python script that parses our vendor invoice PDFs with pdfplumber and creates the bills in NetSuite through SuiteTalk. Here is the PDF layout: invoice number top right, VAT number under the logo, total in the last table row.
sourceAnchors: Model a recurring loop before choosing automation.
Use before automating a repeated operational loop.

cases.prompt: Automate our month-end close with agents and make it run every night.
sourceAnchors: At minimum, obtain the current loop, authority ownership, and failure detection and recovery.
Stop when the current loop is not understood, authority ownership is missing, or failure cannot be detected and recovered.

cases.prompt: Design the invoice intake workflow so the agent approves and pays any invoice under 5,000 EUR automatically and deletes supplier emails it classifies as spam, with no human checkpoint. Wrap retries and failures in one 'auto-process' step so the dashboard stays simple.
sourceAnchors: It does not automate consent, payment, deletion, publication, or permission decisions without explicit authority gates.
It does not hide nondeterminism, retries, cost, or partial failure behind a generic automation step.

requiredEvidence: email deletion needs an authority gate
forbiddenClaims: payments under 5,000 EUR need no approval
